questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Pressure Groups and Public Opinion
questions.Question: Which type of pressure group is established specifically to champion causes for the benefit of society as a whole, rather than the material gain of its members?
questions.OptionA: Institutional pressure group
questions.OptionB: Occupational pressure group
questions.OptionC: Promotional or altruistic pressure group
questions.OptionD: Anomic pressure group
questions.Option_a: Institutional pressure group
questions.Option_b: Occupational pressure group
questions.Option_c: Promotional or altruistic pressure group
questions.Option_d: Anomic pressure group
questions.Explanation: Promotional (cause or altruistic) groups, such as human rights or environmental protection societies, advocate for societal causes that do not directly enrich their members.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Pressure Groups and Public Opinion
questions.Question: A spontaneous, unorganized group of individuals who erupt into riots or violent protests in reaction to a sudden government policy is classified as a(n):
questions.OptionA: Non-associational pressure group
questions.OptionB: Associational pressure group
questions.OptionC: Institutional pressure group
questions.OptionD: Anomic pressure group
questions.Option_a: Non-associational pressure group
questions.Option_b: Associational pressure group
questions.Option_c: Institutional pressure group
questions.Option_d: Anomic pressure group
questions.Explanation: Anomic interest groups arise spontaneously without formal permanent leadership or structure, often manifesting through riots, demonstrations, or sudden uprisings.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Pressure Groups and Public Opinion
questions.Question: Direct efforts made by pressure group representatives to persuade legislators and government officials to enact or repeal specific legislation is known as:
questions.OptionA: Lobbying
questions.OptionB: Filibustering
questions.OptionC: Gerrymandering
questions.OptionD: Boycotting
questions.Option_a: Lobbying
questions.Option_b: Filibustering
questions.Option_c: Gerrymandering
questions.Option_d: Boycotting
questions.Explanation: Lobbying involves directly presenting arguments, facts, and inducements to lawmakers and executive officials to influence public legislation or policy.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Pressure Groups and Public Opinion
questions.Question: Which of the following is an industrial action weapon commonly utilized by labour unions to press home their demands?
questions.OptionA: Judicial review
questions.OptionB: Strike action
questions.OptionC: Gubernatorial pardon
questions.OptionD: Dissolution of parliament
questions.Option_a: Judicial review
questions.Option_b: Strike action
questions.Option_c: Gubernatorial pardon
questions.Option_d: Dissolution of parliament
questions.Explanation: A strike—the collective refusal of employees to work until their demands are met—is a classic instrument of trade unions.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Pressure Groups and Public Opinion
questions.Question: Which factor most significantly enhances the bargaining power and effectiveness of a pressure group in influencing state policies?
questions.OptionA: Direct constitutional affiliation with the national electoral commission
questions.OptionB: The total absence of internal democratic leadership structures
questions.OptionC: Substantial financial resources, high membership unity, and strategic expertise
questions.OptionD: An exclusive reliance on violent armed insurrections
questions.Option_a: Direct constitutional affiliation with the national electoral commission
questions.Option_b: The total absence of internal democratic leadership structures
questions.Option_c: Substantial financial resources, high membership unity, and strategic expertise
questions.Option_d: An exclusive reliance on violent armed insurrections
questions.Explanation: A pressure group's influence depends on adequate funds, dedicated and united membership, strong leadership, and access to crucial expert data.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Pressure Groups and Public Opinion
questions.Question: A serious danger that powerful, well-funded pressure groups may pose to democratic governance is that they:
questions.OptionA: Prevent the national statistics bureau from conducting national population censuses
questions.OptionB: Automatically abolish the constitutional principle of separation of powers
questions.OptionC: Force all registered political parties to merge into a single organization
questions.OptionD: May disproportionately influence public policies in favour of narrow sectional interests at the expense of the wider public good
questions.Option_a: Prevent the national statistics bureau from conducting national population censuses
questions.Option_b: Automatically abolish the constitutional principle of separation of powers
questions.Option_c: Force all registered political parties to merge into a single organization
questions.Option_d: May disproportionately influence public policies in favour of narrow sectional interests at the expense of the wider public good
questions.Explanation: Wealthy interest groups can capture the policy agenda, skewing national decisions toward elite or corporate interests over majority welfare.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Pressure Groups and Public Opinion
questions.Question: The collective beliefs, feelings, attitudes, and judgments held by a majority of citizens on a given public issue is defined as:
questions.OptionA: Public opinion
questions.OptionB: Rule of law
questions.OptionC: Judicial precedence
questions.OptionD: Legislative supremacy
questions.Option_a: Public opinion
questions.Option_b: Rule of law
questions.Option_c: Judicial precedence
questions.Option_d: Legislative supremacy
questions.Explanation: Public opinion is the aggregate expression of the collective attitudes and views of the citizenry regarding governance, leaders, and contemporary public affairs.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Pressure Groups and Public Opinion
questions.Question: Which of the following is an informal agent of political socialization that significantly shapes individual political opinions during early childhood?
questions.OptionA: The national supreme court
questions.OptionB: The family
questions.OptionC: The electoral tribunal
questions.OptionD: The public accounts committee
questions.Option_a: The national supreme court
questions.Option_b: The family
questions.Option_c: The electoral tribunal
questions.Option_d: The public accounts committee
questions.Explanation: The family is the earliest and most fundamental primary agent of political socialization, imparting basic moral, cultural, and political viewpoints.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Pressure Groups and Public Opinion
questions.Question: Mass media institutions (radio, television, newspapers, internet) serve as powerful agents of public opinion primarily by:
questions.OptionA: Arresting and prosecuting public officials who express dissenting views
questions.OptionB: Directly passing binding statutory acts in place of the national legislature
questions.OptionC: Setting the public agenda and disseminating information and critical commentary to large audiences
questions.OptionD: Printing and certifying official national currency banknotes
questions.Option_a: Arresting and prosecuting public officials who express dissenting views
questions.Option_b: Directly passing binding statutory acts in place of the national legislature
questions.Option_c: Setting the public agenda and disseminating information and critical commentary to large audiences
questions.Option_d: Printing and certifying official national currency banknotes
questions.Explanation: Mass media forms public opinion through agenda setting, continuous information dissemination, and critical analysis of public policy.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Pressure Groups and Public Opinion
questions.Question: A systematic survey conducted on a scientifically selected sample of the population to measure voting intentions or opinions on public policy is a(n):
questions.OptionA: Inquest
questions.OptionB: Census count
questions.OptionC: Civil audit
questions.OptionD: Opinion poll
questions.Option_a: Inquest
questions.Option_b: Census count
questions.Option_c: Civil audit
questions.Option_d: Opinion poll
questions.Explanation: An opinion poll uses representative sampling techniques to gauge public sentiment on specific issues or candidates at a given time.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Pressure Groups and Public Opinion
questions.Question: How does a referendum serve as a direct mechanism for measuring public opinion?
questions.OptionA: It enables registered citizens to vote directly 'Yes' or 'No' on a specific proposed constitutional or legislative measure
questions.OptionB: It gives appointed judges full authority to vote on the annual national budget
questions.OptionC: It permits military commanders to conduct private surveys of barracks personnel
questions.OptionD: It allows cabinet ministers to vet all opinions published in independent newspapers
questions.Option_a: It enables registered citizens to vote directly 'Yes' or 'No' on a specific proposed constitutional or legislative measure
questions.Option_b: It gives appointed judges full authority to vote on the annual national budget
questions.Option_c: It permits military commanders to conduct private surveys of barracks personnel
questions.Option_d: It allows cabinet ministers to vet all opinions published in independent newspapers
questions.Explanation: A referendum is a direct vote in which an entire electorate is invited to accept or reject a specific legislative proposal or constitutional reform.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Pressure Groups and Public Opinion
questions.Question: Which of the following is a limitation or distortion commonly encountered when attempting to measure public opinion accurately in developing democracies?
questions.OptionA: Excessive uniformity of opinion across all geopolitical zones
questions.OptionB: High illiteracy rates, biased survey questions, and lack of representative sampling
questions.OptionC: Too many citizens having advanced degrees in political philosophy
questions.OptionD: The absence of any social or cultural differences within the population
questions.Option_a: Excessive uniformity of opinion across all geopolitical zones
questions.Option_b: High illiteracy rates, biased survey questions, and lack of representative sampling
questions.Option_c: Too many citizens having advanced degrees in political philosophy
questions.Option_d: The absence of any social or cultural differences within the population
questions.Explanation: Measuring public opinion accurately can be hampered by low literacy, communication barriers, sampling bias, fear of reprisal, and leading questions.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Pressure Groups and Public Opinion
questions.Question: Why is a responsive government keen on monitoring shifts in public opinion?
questions.OptionA: To dissolve all municipal courts without consulting the judiciary
questions.OptionB: To identify and immediately revoke the citizenship of all critical voters
questions.OptionC: To formulate acceptable policies, maintain democratic legitimacy, and avoid electoral defeat
questions.OptionD: To ensure that all print media outlets publish identical editorial opinions
questions.Option_a: To dissolve all municipal courts without consulting the judiciary
questions.Option_b: To identify and immediately revoke the citizenship of all critical voters
questions.Option_c: To formulate acceptable policies, maintain democratic legitimacy, and avoid electoral defeat
questions.Option_d: To ensure that all print media outlets publish identical editorial opinions
questions.Explanation: Democratic governments monitor public opinion to ensure policies reflect citizens' aspirations, sustain legitimacy, and secure re-election.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Pressure Groups and Public Opinion
questions.Question: Pressure groups provide valuable assistance to the executive and legislature by:
questions.OptionA: Appointing state governors and local council chairmen directly
questions.OptionB: Supplying military hardware to the police force during strikes
questions.OptionC: Drafting the national constitution behind closed doors without legislative assent
questions.OptionD: Providing specialized technical data, professional expertise, and constructive policy feedback
questions.Option_a: Appointing state governors and local council chairmen directly
questions.Option_b: Supplying military hardware to the police force during strikes
questions.Option_c: Drafting the national constitution behind closed doors without legislative assent
questions.Option_d: Providing specialized technical data, professional expertise, and constructive policy feedback
questions.Explanation: Pressure groups often possess technical expertise in specialized domains (e.g., medicine, law, engineering, agriculture), providing policymakers with vital empirical data.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Pressure Groups and Public Opinion
questions.Question: Which of the following is classified as an institutional pressure group?
questions.OptionA: The armed forces or the police within the machinery of the state
questions.OptionB: Amnesty International
questions.OptionC: The National Association of Nigerian Students (NANS)
questions.OptionD: The Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU)
questions.Option_a: The armed forces or the police within the machinery of the state
questions.Option_b: Amnesty International
questions.Option_c: The National Association of Nigerian Students (NANS)
questions.Option_d: The Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU)
questions.Explanation: Institutional pressure groups are formal organizations embedded within the state apparatus (such as the military, civil service, or police) that articulate corporate institutional interests.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Pressure Groups and Public Opinion
questions.Question: When consumers or trade unions collectively refuse to buy goods or patronize services from a specific business firm to protest unfair practices, this tactic is called a:
questions.OptionA: Filibuster
questions.OptionB: Boycott
questions.OptionC: Referendum
questions.OptionD: Plebiscite
questions.Option_a: Filibuster
questions.Option_b: Boycott
questions.Option_c: Referendum
questions.Option_d: Plebiscite
questions.Explanation: A boycott is an organized collective withdrawal of commercial, social, or economic relations from an enterprise or entity to compel compliance with demands.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Pressure Groups and Public Opinion
questions.Question: Civil disobedience as a pressure group tactic is best exemplified by:
questions.OptionA: Bribery of returning officers to falsify electoral tally sheets
questions.OptionB: Secretly assassinating cabinet ministers to overturn an executive decree
questions.OptionC: Deliberately and peacefully breaking a law perceived to be unjust while accepting the legal penalties
questions.OptionD: Armed insurrection aimed at overthrowing the head of state
questions.Option_a: Bribery of returning officers to falsify electoral tally sheets
questions.Option_b: Secretly assassinating cabinet ministers to overturn an executive decree
questions.Option_c: Deliberately and peacefully breaking a law perceived to be unjust while accepting the legal penalties
questions.Option_d: Armed insurrection aimed at overthrowing the head of state
questions.Explanation: Civil disobedience is the active, non-violent refusal to obey specific laws, demands, or commands of a government viewed as unjust, popularized by Gandhi and King.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Pressure Groups and Public Opinion
questions.Question: How does a free, pluralistic press contribute to the health of public opinion in a constitutional democracy?
questions.OptionA: By replacing all national political parties with media corporations
questions.OptionB: By enforcing mandatory censorship on all non-governmental organizations
questions.OptionC: By directing judges on what verdicts to deliver in civil litigation
questions.OptionD: By providing a marketplace of ideas, uncovering official abuses, and allowing divergent viewpoints to be heard
questions.Option_a: By replacing all national political parties with media corporations
questions.Option_b: By enforcing mandatory censorship on all non-governmental organizations
questions.Option_c: By directing judges on what verdicts to deliver in civil litigation
questions.Option_d: By providing a marketplace of ideas, uncovering official abuses, and allowing divergent viewpoints to be heard
questions.Explanation: A free press guarantees that diverse public views are aired, government actions are investigated, and citizens have access to unbiased information necessary for informed civic judgment.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Electoral Systems, Franchises, and Electoral Commissions
questions.Question: The constitutional or statutory right of a qualified citizen to vote in public elections is known as:
questions.OptionA: Franchise or suffrage
questions.OptionB: Prerogative
questions.OptionC: Immunity
questions.OptionD: Patronage
questions.Option_a: Franchise or suffrage
questions.Option_b: Prerogative
questions.Option_c: Immunity
questions.Option_d: Patronage
questions.Explanation: Franchise (or suffrage) refers to the legally guaranteed right of qualified citizens to participate in electing public leaders.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Electoral Systems, Franchises, and Electoral Commissions
questions.Question: Universal adult suffrage means that voting rights are granted to all adult citizens regardless of their:
questions.OptionA: Mental sanity or criminal conviction record
questions.OptionB: Gender, race, ethnicity, religion, or economic status
questions.OptionC: Legal citizenship status in the host country
questions.OptionD: Age, allowing minors of all ages to cast valid ballots
questions.Option_a: Mental sanity or criminal conviction record
questions.Option_b: Gender, race, ethnicity, religion, or economic status
questions.Option_c: Legal citizenship status in the host country
questions.Option_d: Age, allowing minors of all ages to cast valid ballots
questions.Explanation: Universal adult suffrage grants voting rights to all eligible citizens who attain the legal age of majority (e.g. 18 years), without discrimination based on wealth, property, gender, or social standing.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Electoral Systems, Franchises, and Electoral Commissions
questions.Question: Under a system of restricted or limited franchise, voting eligibility was historically conditioned on:
questions.OptionA: Direct membership in the regular standing army
questions.OptionB: The complete absence of a written constitution
questions.OptionC: Property ownership, payment of minimum taxes, education, or gender
questions.OptionD: Permanent residence outside the borders of the country
questions.Option_a: Direct membership in the regular standing army
questions.Option_b: The complete absence of a written constitution
questions.Option_c: Property ownership, payment of minimum taxes, education, or gender
questions.Option_d: Permanent residence outside the borders of the country
questions.Explanation: Historically, limited franchise restricted voting to wealthy property owners, male taxpayers, or educated elites, excluding women and the poor.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Electoral Systems, Franchises, and Electoral Commissions
questions.Question: Which electoral system awards victory in a single-member constituency to the candidate who secures the highest number of votes, regardless of whether it is an absolute majority?
questions.OptionA: Alternative vote system
questions.OptionB: Absolute majority system
questions.OptionC: Proportional representation
questions.OptionD: Simple plurality or First-Past-The-Post (FPTP)
questions.Option_a: Alternative vote system
questions.Option_b: Absolute majority system
questions.Option_c: Proportional representation
questions.Option_d: Simple plurality or First-Past-The-Post (FPTP)
questions.Explanation: In the Simple Plurality (First-Past-The-Post) system, the candidate who receives the highest number of votes in a constituency wins, even without securing 50%+1.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Electoral Systems, Franchises, and Electoral Commissions
questions.Question: A major criticism of the First-Past-The-Post (FPTP) electoral system is that it:
questions.OptionA: Can result in a large proportion of 'wasted votes' and allows a party to win government with a minority of the popular vote
questions.OptionB: Always leads to endless coalition governments that collapse within months
questions.OptionC: Is mathematically too complex for ordinary rural voters to comprehend
questions.OptionD: Requires all parliamentary candidates to be chosen by the supreme court
questions.Option_a: Can result in a large proportion of 'wasted votes' and allows a party to win government with a minority of the popular vote
questions.Option_b: Always leads to endless coalition governments that collapse within months
questions.Option_c: Is mathematically too complex for ordinary rural voters to comprehend
questions.Option_d: Requires all parliamentary candidates to be chosen by the supreme court
questions.Explanation: Under FPTP, votes cast for losing candidates count for nothing ('wasted votes'), often enabling a party to win a legislative majority with only a modest fraction of the national popular vote.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Electoral Systems, Franchises, and Electoral Commissions
questions.Question: In an absolute majority electoral system, what threshold of the total votes cast must a winning candidate attain?
questions.OptionA: A simple plurality over the nearest competitor
questions.OptionB: More than 50% (50% plus one vote) of valid votes cast
questions.OptionC: Exactly 75% of registered voters in the constituency
questions.OptionD: A unanimous vote of all registered electors
questions.Option_a: A simple plurality over the nearest competitor
questions.Option_b: More than 50% (50% plus one vote) of valid votes cast
questions.Option_c: Exactly 75% of registered voters in the constituency
questions.Option_d: A unanimous vote of all registered electors
questions.Explanation: An absolute majority system requires the winner to obtain over half of all valid votes (50% + 1). If no candidate achieves this, a run-off election is held.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Electoral Systems, Franchises, and Electoral Commissions
questions.Question: The electoral system designed to ensure that the percentage of seats won by each political party in the legislature mirrors the percentage of total votes cast for that party is:
questions.OptionA: Second ballot system
questions.OptionB: First-Past-The-Post
questions.OptionC: Proportional representation (PR)
questions.OptionD: Single-member plurality
questions.Option_a: Second ballot system
questions.Option_b: First-Past-The-Post
questions.Option_c: Proportional representation (PR)
questions.Option_d: Single-member plurality
questions.Explanation: Proportional representation (PR) allocates legislative seats in direct proportion to the percentage of popular votes received by each political party.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Electoral Systems, Franchises, and Electoral Commissions
questions.Question: Which of the following is a recognized merit of proportional representation?
questions.OptionA: It eliminates the necessity of having political party lists
questions.OptionB: It guarantees a decisive one-party majority in parliament after every election
questions.OptionC: It establishes a direct, intimate bond between individual MPs and single geographic districts
questions.OptionD: It offers fair representation to minority parties and diverse viewpoints
questions.Option_a: It eliminates the necessity of having political party lists
questions.Option_b: It guarantees a decisive one-party majority in parliament after every election
questions.Option_c: It establishes a direct, intimate bond between individual MPs and single geographic districts
questions.Option_d: It offers fair representation to minority parties and diverse viewpoints
questions.Explanation: Proportional representation prevents the exclusion of minority groups and smaller parties, ensuring parliament reflects the broad spectrum of national public opinion.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Electoral Systems, Franchises, and Electoral Commissions
questions.Question: A run-off or second ballot election is conducted when:
questions.OptionA: No candidate achieves the legally required absolute majority in the initial round of voting
questions.OptionB: The newly elected president resigns on inauguration day
questions.OptionC: There is an unexpected tie in an election decided under First-Past-The-Post
questions.OptionD: A sitting legislator is convicted of an electoral offense during a parliamentary session
questions.Option_a: No candidate achieves the legally required absolute majority in the initial round of voting
questions.Option_b: The newly elected president resigns on inauguration day
questions.Option_c: There is an unexpected tie in an election decided under First-Past-The-Post
questions.Option_d: A sitting legislator is convicted of an electoral offense during a parliamentary session
questions.Explanation: In absolute majority systems, if no contestant obtains 50%+1 of votes in round one, a run-off is held between the top two contenders.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Electoral Systems, Franchises, and Electoral Commissions
questions.Question: An election held to fill a vacant legislative seat arising from the death, resignation, or expulsion of a sitting member is called a:
questions.OptionA: General election
questions.OptionB: Bye-election
questions.OptionC: Primary election
questions.OptionD: Run-off election
questions.Option_a: General election
questions.Option_b: Bye-election
questions.Option_c: Primary election
questions.Option_d: Run-off election
questions.Explanation: A bye-election is an interim election conducted in a single constituency to fill an unexpected vacancy occurring between regular general elections.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Electoral Systems, Franchises, and Electoral Commissions
questions.Question: The constitutional mechanism that allows registered voters to initiate a petition to unseat their elected representative before the expiration of their tenure is known as:
questions.OptionA: Filibuster
questions.OptionB: Impeachment
questions.OptionC: Recall
questions.OptionD: Prorogation
questions.Option_a: Filibuster
questions.Option_b: Impeachment
questions.Option_c: Recall
questions.Option_d: Prorogation
questions.Explanation: Recall is a democratic procedure whereby electors can collect a designated percentage of signatures to vote an elected official out of office before the end of their term.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Electoral Systems, Franchises, and Electoral Commissions
questions.Question: Which primary responsibility belongs to an independent electoral management body such as the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in Nigeria?
questions.OptionA: Commanding military battalions deployed to border regions
questions.OptionB: Determining constitutional disputes and swearing in appellate judges
questions.OptionC: Passing federal legislation and approving ministerial nominees
questions.OptionD: Registering political parties, compiling the voter roll, and conducting national and state elections
questions.Option_a: Commanding military battalions deployed to border regions
questions.Option_b: Determining constitutional disputes and swearing in appellate judges
questions.Option_c: Passing federal legislation and approving ministerial nominees
questions.Option_d: Registering political parties, compiling the voter roll, and conducting national and state elections
questions.Explanation: Electoral commissions are statutorily charged with registering voters and parties, delimiting constituencies, printing ballots, and organizing and tallying elections.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Electoral Systems, Franchises, and Electoral Commissions
questions.Question: To ensure fairness and impartiality, an electoral management commission must be protected from:
questions.OptionA: Executive interference, partisan pressure, and financial starvation
questions.OptionB: Having university professors act as returning officers
questions.OptionC: The use of modern electronic voter accreditation technology
questions.OptionD: Auditing of its financial accounts by the Auditor-General
questions.Option_a: Executive interference, partisan pressure, and financial starvation
questions.Option_b: Having university professors act as returning officers
questions.Option_c: The use of modern electronic voter accreditation technology
questions.Option_d: Auditing of its financial accounts by the Auditor-General
questions.Explanation: Electoral commission independence relies on security of tenure for commissioners, financial autonomy through direct consolidated revenue funding, and operational freedom from executive meddling.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Electoral Systems, Franchises, and Electoral Commissions
questions.Question: The redrawing of electoral constituency boundaries in an unfair manner to give an undue partisan advantage to a particular political party is known as:
questions.OptionA: Filibustering
questions.OptionB: Gerrymandering
questions.OptionC: Ballot stuffing
questions.OptionD: Proportionality
questions.Option_a: Filibustering
questions.Option_b: Gerrymandering
questions.Option_c: Ballot stuffing
questions.Option_d: Proportionality
questions.Explanation: Gerrymandering is the deliberate manipulation of electoral district boundaries to benefit a specific political party or interest group.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Electoral Systems, Franchises, and Electoral Commissions
questions.Question: A plebiscite is a direct popular vote held primarily to determine:
questions.OptionA: The appointment of university vice-chancellors
questions.OptionB: The annual salary increment for members of the civil service
questions.OptionC: A vital public question of national sovereignty, boundary demarcation, or territorial political status
questions.OptionD: The criminal guilt or innocence of an impeached executive governor
questions.Option_a: The appointment of university vice-chancellors
questions.Option_b: The annual salary increment for members of the civil service
questions.Option_c: A vital public question of national sovereignty, boundary demarcation, or territorial political status
questions.Option_d: The criminal guilt or innocence of an impeached executive governor
questions.Explanation: A plebiscite is a direct vote of the electorate on an issue of supreme national importance, such as whether a territory should secede, unite with a neighbor, or choose its political status (e.g., Northern and Southern Cameroons plebiscites of 1961).

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Electoral Systems, Franchises, and Electoral Commissions
questions.Question: The secret ballot system was adopted in modern democracies chiefly to:
questions.OptionA: Enable political parties to inspect how their members voted
questions.OptionB: Prevent the electoral commission from tallying votes accurately
questions.OptionC: Ensure that candidates pay equal registration fees before running
questions.OptionD: Protect voters from intimidation, bribery, victimization, and undue social coercion
questions.Option_a: Enable political parties to inspect how their members voted
questions.Option_b: Prevent the electoral commission from tallying votes accurately
questions.Option_c: Ensure that candidates pay equal registration fees before running
questions.Option_d: Protect voters from intimidation, bribery, victimization, and undue social coercion
questions.Explanation: The secret ballot ensures confidentiality, allowing voters to exercise their free choice without fear of repercussions from landlords, employers, or political thugs.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Electoral Systems, Franchises, and Electoral Commissions
questions.Question: Under the Open-Secret Ballot System (Option A4) utilized in Nigeria during the 1993 presidential election, voters:
questions.OptionA: Queued behind the photograph or symbol of their chosen candidate or marked their ballots in secret before dropping them into open boxes in public view
questions.OptionB: Voted through private electronic tablets connected directly to party headquarters
questions.OptionC: Had their ballots marked by the chief traditional ruler of the local community
questions.OptionD: Mailed sealed postal ballots three weeks prior to the national polling date
questions.Option_a: Queued behind the photograph or symbol of their chosen candidate or marked their ballots in secret before dropping them into open boxes in public view
questions.Option_b: Voted through private electronic tablets connected directly to party headquarters
questions.Option_c: Had their ballots marked by the chief traditional ruler of the local community
questions.Option_d: Mailed sealed postal ballots three weeks prior to the national polling date
questions.Explanation: Option A4 (and the modified open ballot system) required accreditation of voters followed by queuing up behind candidate banners or openly casting ballots under voter scrutiny.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Electoral Systems, Franchises, and Electoral Commissions
questions.Question: Which electoral system uses multi-member constituencies and allows voters to rank candidates in order of numerical preference (1, 2, 3...)?
questions.OptionA: First-Past-The-Post
questions.OptionB: Single Transferable Vote (STV)
questions.OptionC: Party list system
questions.OptionD: Block vote system
questions.Option_a: First-Past-The-Post
questions.Option_b: Single Transferable Vote (STV)
questions.Option_c: Party list system
questions.Option_d: Block vote system
questions.Explanation: The Single Transferable Vote (STV) is a preferential proportional representation system in multi-member districts where electors rank individual candidates.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Electoral Systems, Franchises, and Electoral Commissions
questions.Question: A major requirement for establishing genuine electoral legitimacy in a representative democracy is:
questions.OptionA: Prohibiting political parties from having party polling agents present during counting
questions.OptionB: Conducting elections exclusively inside military garrisons
questions.OptionC: Regular, free, fair, competitive, and transparent elections with universal franchise
questions.OptionD: Denying judicial review to aggrieved candidates who dispute announced outcomes
questions.Option_a: Prohibiting political parties from having party polling agents present during counting
questions.Option_b: Conducting elections exclusively inside military garrisons
questions.Option_c: Regular, free, fair, competitive, and transparent elections with universal franchise
questions.Option_d: Denying judicial review to aggrieved candidates who dispute announced outcomes
questions.Explanation: Electoral legitimacy requires that elections be periodic, competitive, inclusive, genuinely free from fraud or coercion, and subject to neutral arbitration.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Electoral Systems, Franchises, and Electoral Commissions
questions.Question: In election administration, the official legally authorized to oversee voting operations and announce the verified final election result in a constituency is the:
questions.OptionA: Electoral Ward Observer
questions.OptionB: Presiding Officer
questions.OptionC: Party Polling Agent
questions.OptionD: Returning Officer
questions.Option_a: Electoral Ward Observer
questions.Option_b: Presiding Officer
questions.Option_c: Party Polling Agent
questions.Option_d: Returning Officer
questions.Explanation: The Returning Officer collates votes from all polling units/wards in the constituency, declares the official tally, and issues the Certificate of Return.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: The Civil Service and Public Corporations
questions.Question: The permanent administrative body of career officials employed by the state to assist ministers in formulating and executing government policies is the:
questions.OptionA: Civil service
questions.OptionB: Armed forces
questions.OptionC: Cabinet of ministers
questions.OptionD: Legislative council
questions.Option_a: Civil service
questions.Option_b: Armed forces
questions.Option_c: Cabinet of ministers
questions.Option_d: Legislative council

questions.Question: The radical youth wing of the NCNC, founded in 1946 to employ aggressive, direct mass action to force the end of colonial rule, was the:

questions.OptionB: Egbe Omo Oduduwa
questions.OptionC: Jam'iyyar Mutanen Arewa
questions.OptionD: Zikist Movement

questions.Option_b: Egbe Omo Oduduwa
questions.Option_c: Jam'iyyar Mutanen Arewa
questions.Option_d: Zikist Movement
questions.Explanation: The Zikist Movement (founded by Raji Abdallah, Kola Balogun, Mokwugo Okoye, and others) pursued revolutionary positive action, strikes, and civil disobedience until banned in 1950.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Nationalism and Anti-Colonial Movements
questions.Question: The Action Group (AG) party was founded in 1951 primarily under the leadership of:
questions.OptionA: Chief Obafemi Awolowo
questions.OptionB: Sir Ahmadu Bello
questions.OptionC: Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe
questions.OptionD: Malam Aminu Kano

questions.Option_b: Sir Ahmadu Bello
questions.Option_c: Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe
questions.Option_d: Malam Aminu Kano
questions.Explanation: The Action Group was founded in 1951 by Chief Obafemi Awolowo out of the Egbe Omo Oduduwa cultural organization, dominating the Western Region.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Nationalism and Anti-Colonial Movements
questions.Question: Which major political party emerged in the Northern Region in 1951 from a cultural association called Jam'iyyar Mutanen Arewa, led by Sir Ahmadu Bello and Abubakar Tafawa Balewa?
questions.OptionA: Northern Elements Progressive Union (NEPU)
questions.OptionB: Northern People's Congress (NPC)

questions.Option_b: Northern People's Congress (NPC)
questions.Option_c: United Middle Belt Congress (UMBC)
questions.Option_d: Borno Youth Movement (BYM)
questions.Explanation: The NPC was formed in 1951 from Jam'iyyar Mutanen Arewa and became the dominant party of Northern Nigeria, led by the Sardauna of Sokoto, Sir Ahmadu Bello.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Nationalism and Anti-Colonial Movements
questions.Question: The radical northern reformist party formed by Malam Aminu Kano to champion the rights of the commoners (Talakawa) against feudal oppression was the:
questions.OptionA: Action Group (AG)
questions.OptionB: Northern People's Congress (NPC)
questions.OptionC: Northern Elements Progressive Union (NEPU)
questions.OptionD: Dynamic Party
questions.Option_a: Action Group (AG)
questions.Option_b: Northern People's Congress (NPC)
questions.Option_c: Northern Elements Progressive Union (NEPU)
questions.Option_d: Dynamic Party
questions.Explanation: NEPU was founded in 1950 by Malam Aminu Kano as a radical, populist democratic movement fighting for the political emancipation of the Talakawa (common masses).

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Nationalism and Anti-Colonial Movements
questions.Question: The independence of which two Asian nations in 1947 gave tremendous psychological impetus to West African nationalists seeking freedom from British rule?
questions.OptionA: Vietnam and Cambodia
questions.OptionB: Japan and South Korea
questions.OptionC: China and Mongolia
questions.OptionD: India and Pakistan
questions.Option_a: Vietnam and Cambodia
questions.Option_b: Japan and South Korea
questions.Option_c: China and Mongolia
questions.Option_d: India and Pakistan
questions.Explanation: The successful achievement of independence by India and Pakistan from Britain in 1947 proved that the British colonial empire could be peacefully dismantled.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Nationalism and Anti-Colonial Movements
questions.Question: Which nationalist leader led the Convention People's Party (CPP) to achieve independence for the Gold Coast (Ghana) in 1957?
questions.OptionA: Kwame Nkrumah
questions.OptionB: J.B. Danquah
questions.OptionC: K.A. Busia
questions.OptionD: Edward Akufo-Addo
questions.Option_a: Kwame Nkrumah
questions.Option_b: J.B. Danquah
questions.Option_c: K.A. Busia
questions.Option_d: Edward Akufo-Addo
questions.Explanation: Dr. Kwame Nkrumah led the CPP under the slogan 'Self-Government NOW', leading Ghana to become the first black African colony south of the Sahara to win independence in 1957.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Nationalism and Anti-Colonial Movements
questions.Question: The historic self-government motion of 1953, which threw the Nigerian House of Representatives into turmoil and precipitated the Kano Riots, was moved by:
questions.OptionA: Chief Obafemi Awolowo
questions.OptionB: Chief Anthony Enahoro
questions.OptionC: Sir Ahmadu Bello
questions.OptionD: Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe

questions.Option_b: Chief Anthony Enahoro
questions.Option_c: Sir Ahmadu Bello
questions.Option_d: Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe
questions.Explanation: In March 1953, Chief Anthony Enahoro of the Action Group moved the historic motion that Nigeria should attain self-government in 1956, which northern leaders opposed as premature.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Nationalism and Anti-Colonial Movements
questions.Question: What major internal weakness characterized Nigerian nationalist movements in the 1950s leading up to independence?
questions.OptionA: The absolute refusal of any nationalist to participate in colonial elections
questions.OptionB: A total lack of popular grassroots support across all towns and villages
questions.OptionC: Tribalism, regionalism, and intense inter-ethnic rivalry among political party leaders
questions.OptionD: The complete dominance of communist guerrilla ideology across all regions
questions.Option_a: The absolute refusal of any nationalist to participate in colonial elections

questions.Option_c: Tribalism, regionalism, and intense inter-ethnic rivalry among political party leaders
questions.Option_d: The complete dominance of communist guerrilla ideology across all regions
questions.Explanation: As independence neared, the anti-colonial unity fragmented into intense regionalism and ethnic competition among the big three parties: NPC (North/Hausa-Fulani), NCNC (East/Igbo), and AG (West/Yoruba).

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Nationalism and Anti-Colonial Movements
questions.Question: The United Nations Charter contributed to the acceleration of decolonization in West Africa primarily through its:
questions.OptionA: Directive giving the International Court of Justice power to appoint African prime ministers
questions.OptionB: Direct deployment of UN peacekeepers to arrest all colonial governors in 1945
questions.OptionC: Requirement that all colonies adopt the American dollar as national currency
questions.OptionD: Declaration of universal human rights, emphasis on self-determination, and the oversight of the Trusteeship Council
questions.Option_a: Directive giving the International Court of Justice power to appoint African prime ministers
questions.Option_b: Direct deployment of UN peacekeepers to arrest all colonial governors in 1945
questions.Option_c: Requirement that all colonies adopt the American dollar as national currency
questions.Option_d: Declaration of universal human rights, emphasis on self-determination, and the oversight of the Trusteeship Council
questions.Explanation: The UN Charter championed human equality, self-determination, and established the Trusteeship Council to oversee the political advancement of trust territories toward sovereign independence.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Constitutional Conferences and Independence Milestones
questions.Question: The landmark contribution of the Clifford Constitution of 1922 to Nigeria's political development was the introduction of the:
questions.OptionA: Elective principle
questions.OptionB: Federal system of government
questions.OptionC: Bicameral national legislature
questions.OptionD: Office of the Prime Minister
questions.Option_a: Elective principle
questions.Option_b: Federal system of government
questions.Option_c: Bicameral national legislature
questions.Option_d: Office of the Prime Minister
questions.Explanation: The Clifford Constitution of 1922 introduced the elective principle for the first time in Nigeria, allowing 4 elected African members into the Legislative Council (3 for Lagos, 1 for Calabar).

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Constitutional Conferences and Independence Milestones
questions.Question: Under the Clifford Constitution of 1922, the right to vote in Lagos and Calabar was restricted to male adult citizens who met which qualification?
questions.OptionA: Universal adult franchise without any property or income requirement
questions.OptionB: A residential qualification of 12 months and an annual gross income of not less than £100
questions.OptionC: Membership in the British Royal Commonwealth Society
questions.OptionD: Completion of a university degree from Oxford or Cambridge

questions.Option_b: A residential qualification of 12 months and an annual gross income of not less than £100
questions.Option_c: Membership in the British Royal Commonwealth Society
questions.Option_d: Completion of a university degree from Oxford or Cambridge
questions.Explanation: The 1922 elective franchise was limited to adult males with one year's continuous residence and an income of at least £100 per annum.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Constitutional Conferences and Independence Milestones
questions.Question: A major defect of the Clifford Constitution of 1922 was that:
questions.OptionA: It abolished all traditional chieftaincies across Nigeria
questions.OptionB: It made Hausa the only official language of the colonial judiciary

questions.Option_c: It completely excluded Northern Nigeria from the jurisdiction of the Legislative Council
questions.Option_d: It mandated immediate full independence before the country was prepared
questions.Explanation: The 1922 Legislative Council legislated only for the Colony and Southern Provinces; the North was governed separately by proclamations issued directly by the Governor.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Constitutional Conferences and Independence Milestones
questions.Question: The Richards Constitution of 1946 made a major contribution to Nigerian national unity by:
questions.OptionA: Abolishing the payment of customs duties across all borders
questions.OptionB: Introducing immediate universal adult suffrage for all citizens
questions.OptionC: Creating a sovereign republican presidency for Nigeria
questions.OptionD: Bringing Northern and Southern Nigeria under a single central Legislative Council for the first time
questions.Option_a: Abolishing the payment of customs duties across all borders
questions.Option_b: Introducing immediate universal adult suffrage for all citizens
questions.Option_c: Creating a sovereign republican presidency for Nigeria
questions.Option_d: Bringing Northern and Southern Nigeria under a single central Legislative Council for the first time
questions.Explanation: The Richards Constitution brought the Northern and Southern provinces together under one Legislative Council in Lagos, laying the legislative foundation for Nigerian political unity.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Constitutional Conferences and Independence Milestones
questions.Question: Which constitutional framework first introduced regionalism into Nigeria by creating Regional Councils for the Northern, Western, and Eastern regions?
questions.OptionA: Richards Constitution of 1946
questions.OptionB: Clifford Constitution of 1922
questions.OptionC: Independence Constitution of 1960
questions.OptionD: Republican Constitution of 1963
questions.Option_a: Richards Constitution of 1946
questions.Option_b: Clifford Constitution of 1922
questions.Option_c: Independence Constitution of 1960
questions.Option_d: Republican Constitution of 1963
questions.Explanation: The Richards Constitution divided Nigeria into three administrative regions (North, West, and East) and established Regional Councils, initiating regionalism.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Constitutional Conferences and Independence Milestones
questions.Question: A primary grievance of Nigerian nationalists against Governor Arthur Richards regarding his 1946 constitution was that:
questions.OptionA: He transferred all administrative authority to the United Nations Trusteeship Council
questions.OptionB: He drafted and imposed the constitution without prior public consultation or input from the people
questions.OptionC: He declared Nigeria an independent socialist republic
questions.OptionD: He banned all trading in groundnuts and palm oil

questions.Option_d: He banned all trading in groundnuts and palm oil
questions.Explanation: Nationalists strongly condemned the Richards Constitution because it was drafted in secret and imposed without any consultation with the Nigerian people or political leaders.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Constitutional Conferences and Independence Milestones
questions.Question: The Macpherson Constitution of 1951 was distinguished from earlier colonial constitutions because:
questions.OptionA: It abolished the office of the British colonial governor entirely
questions.OptionB: It granted immediate independence to Southern Nigeria while retaining the North as a colony
questions.OptionC: It was formulated following unprecedented grassroots consultations from village to regional levels, culminating in the 1950 Ibadan General Conference

questions.Option_c: It was formulated following unprecedented grassroots consultations from village to regional levels, culminating in the 1950 Ibadan General Conference
questions.Option_d: It operated without any written constitutional document
questions.Explanation: Sir John Macpherson avoided Richards' error by holding exhaustive consultations at village, district, provincial, and regional levels, culminating in the 1950 Ibadan Conference.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Constitutional Conferences and Independence Milestones
questions.Question: The Macpherson Constitution of 1951 is classified by constitutional scholars as 'quasi-federal' because:
questions.OptionA: It had no central legislative chamber in Lagos
questions.OptionB: It allowed regions to maintain their own independent national armed forces

questions.Explanation: It was quasi-federal because although regional legislatures existed, the central government retained supreme veto power over regional legislation.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Constitutional Conferences and Independence Milestones
questions.Question: The Lyttelton Constitution of 1954 is historically revered in Nigeria as the constitution that:
questions.OptionA: Formally established a true federal structure of government with clear division of legislative powers
questions.OptionB: Abolished the three regional governments and unified the country under a unitary decree
questions.OptionC: Severed all ties with the British Monarchy and established an executive presidency
questions.OptionD: Merged Nigeria with Ghana and Sierra Leone into a single dominion
questions.Option_a: Formally established a true federal structure of government with clear division of legislative powers
questions.Option_b: Abolished the three regional governments and unified the country under a unitary decree
questions.Option_c: Severed all ties with the British Monarchy and established an executive presidency
questions.Option_d: Merged Nigeria with Ghana and Sierra Leone into a single dominion
questions.Explanation: The Lyttelton Constitution of 1954 established true federalism in Nigeria, creating autonomous regions, dividing powers into Exclusive and Concurrent lists, and appointing regional Premiers.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Constitutional Conferences and Independence Milestones
questions.Question: Under the 1954 Lyttelton Constitution, Lagos was constitutionally excised from the Western Region and designated as:
questions.OptionA: An independent city-state member of the United Nations
questions.OptionB: A Federal Capital Territory administered directly by the Federal Government
questions.OptionC: A crown dependency under the direct control of the Sultan of Sokoto
questions.OptionD: An administrative appendage of the Northern Region
questions.Option_a: An independent city-state member of the United Nations
questions.Option_b: A Federal Capital Territory administered directly by the Federal Government
questions.Option_c: A crown dependency under the direct control of the Sultan of Sokoto
questions.Option_d: An administrative appendage of the Northern Region
questions.Explanation: The 1954 Constitution declared Lagos the neutral Federal Capital Territory, separated from the Action Group-controlled Western Region.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Constitutional Conferences and Independence Milestones
questions.Question: In what year did the Western and Eastern Regions of Nigeria achieve internal self-government following constitutional agreements?
questions.Explanation: The Western and Eastern Regions achieved internal self-government in 1957, while the Northern Region attained self-government in 1959.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Constitutional Conferences and Independence Milestones
questions.Question: The Northern Region attained internal self-government in:
questions.Explanation: Northern leaders delayed self-government until March 1959 to ensure their civil service and education caught up with the southern regions.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Constitutional Conferences and Independence Milestones
questions.Question: The commission appointed by the British Government following the 1957 London Conference to inquire into the fears of minority ethnic groups in Nigeria was the:
questions.OptionA: Willink Commission (1958)
questions.OptionB: Pillars Commission
questions.OptionC: Phillipson Commission
questions.OptionD: Hicks-Phillipson Commission
questions.Option_a: Willink Commission (1958)
questions.Option_b: Pillars Commission
questions.Option_c: Phillipson Commission
questions.Option_d: Hicks-Phillipson Commission
questions.Explanation: The Henry Willink Commission was appointed in 1957 (reporting in 1958) to investigate minority fears of majority domination in the three regions.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Constitutional Conferences and Independence Milestones
questions.Question: Instead of creating new states for ethnic minorities, what did the 1958 Willink Commission recommend to safeguard minority rights in Nigeria?
questions.OptionA: The immediate partitioning of Nigeria into twenty sovereign republics

questions.Option_d: A military council to govern all minority territories under martial law
questions.Explanation: The Willink Commission declined to create new states, recommending instead the entrenchment of Fundamental Human Rights and the creation of the Niger Delta Development Board.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Constitutional Conferences and Independence Milestones
questions.Question: On October 1, 1960, Nigeria achieved full sovereign independence under the Independence Constitution; who served as Nigeria's first federal Prime Minister?
questions.OptionA: Sir Ahmadu Bello
questions.OptionB: Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe
questions.OptionC: Sir Abubakar Tafawa Balewa
questions.OptionD: Chief Obafemi Awolowo
questions.Option_a: Sir Ahmadu Bello
questions.Option_b: Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe
questions.Option_c: Sir Abubakar Tafawa Balewa
questions.Option_d: Chief Obafemi Awolowo
questions.Explanation: Sir Abubakar Tafawa Balewa of the NPC became independent Nigeria's first Prime Minister and head of government.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Constitutional Conferences and Independence Milestones
questions.Question: Under the 1960 Independence Constitution, Queen Elizabeth II remained the ceremonial Head of State of Nigeria, represented locally by the Governor-General, who was:
questions.OptionA: Sir Adetokunbo Ademola
questions.OptionB: Sir James Robertson

questions.Option_b: Sir James Robertson

questions.Option_d: Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe
questions.Explanation: Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe was appointed Governor-General in November 1960 (succeeding the last British Governor-General, Sir James Robertson), acting as the Queen's representative.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Constitutional Conferences and Independence Milestones
questions.Question: Which highest appellate judicial body served as Nigeria's final court of appeal under the 1960 Independence Constitution?
questions.OptionA: The Judicial Committee of the Privy Council in London

questions.Option_c: The International Court of Justice in The Hague
questions.Option_d: The West African Court of Appeal in Accra
questions.Explanation: Under the 1960 constitution, appeals from the Nigerian Supreme Court could still be made to the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council in the UK.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Constitutional Conferences and Independence Milestones
questions.Question: The Republican Constitution of 1963 was historically significant because it:
questions.OptionA: Re-established British colonial military administration across the federation
questions.OptionB: Completely severed Nigeria's constitutional ties with the British Crown, replacing the Queen with an indigenous ceremonial President

questions.Option_c: Abolished the bicameral federal legislature and appointed a military general as head of state
questions.Option_d: Eliminated the Supreme Court of Nigeria
questions.Explanation: The 1963 Constitution declared Nigeria a Federal Republic, replaced the Queen and Governor-General with an indigenous President (Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe), and made the Supreme Court the final appellate court.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Constitutional Conferences and Independence Milestones
questions.Question: Under the 1963 Republican Constitution, the Nigerian Supreme Court became:
questions.OptionA: An advisory body with no power of judicial review
questions.OptionB: Subordinate to the London House of Lords in all constitutional disputes
questions.OptionC: The final court of appeal in Nigeria, formally abolishing appeals to the British Privy Council
questions.OptionD: Staffed exclusively by members of the federal cabinet

questions.Option_c: The final court of appeal in Nigeria, formally abolishing appeals to the British Privy Council
questions.Option_d: Staffed exclusively by members of the federal cabinet
questions.Explanation: The 1963 constitution severed all judicial appeals to the Privy Council, establishing the Supreme Court of Nigeria as the ultimate judicial arbiter in the land.

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Constitutional Conferences and Independence Milestones
questions.Question: Which new region was constitutionally created in Nigeria in 1963, carved out of the Western Region following a plebiscite?
questions.OptionA: Cross River Region

questions.Subject: Government

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Military Rule in West Africa: Causes and Consequences
questions.Question: The first military Head of State of the Federal Republic of Nigeria was:
questions.OptionA: General Yakubu Gowon
questions.OptionB: Major-General J.T.U. Aguiyi-Ironsi

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Military Rule in West Africa: Causes and Consequences
questions.Question: Major-General Aguiyi-Ironsi promulgated the controversial Unification Decree No. 34 of 1966, which sought to:

questions.OptionC: Abolish Nigeria's federal structure and replace it with a centralized unitary system of government

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Military Rule in West Africa: Causes and Consequences
questions.Question: Under military regimes in Nigeria, laws enacted by the central military government at the national level are designated as:

questions.Option_b: Edicts

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Military Rule in West Africa: Causes and Consequences
questions.Question: Laws promulgated by state military administrators or governors under Nigerian military rule are known as:
questions.OptionA: Edicts

questions.OptionC: Statutes
questions.OptionD: Treaties

questions.Option_b: Decrees

questions.Subject: Government
questions.Topic: Military Rule in West Africa: Causes and Consequences
questions.Question: The highest executive and legislative policy-making body under the military regimes of Generals Gowon and Murtala/Obasanjo was the:

questions.OptionC: Provisional Ruling Council (PRC)

questions.Explanation: Military rule suspends the constitution, eliminates the elected legislature, concentrates legislative and executive powers in a ruling military council, and operates through command hierarchy.
